messages.subject: Anyone experiencing problems on Windows 8.1 64bit?
messages.body_plain:
On Windows 8.1 64 bit, ggvis does not seem to draw input_slider in the right location. Did anyone else experience this problem?

For instance, if I run the code from one of the vignettes,

library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)

mtcars %>%
    ggvis(~wt, ~mpg) %>%
    layer_smooths(span = input_slider(0.5, 1, value = 1)) %>%
    layer_points(size := input_slider(100, 1000, value = 100))

the plot looks like this. As you can see the input sliders are squeezed and located on the left hand side of the plot. It looks the same even if I display the plot in Chrome as well.

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-xUb3uGPJlZ0/VSGoPDgxoJI/AAAAAAAABCA/oyAjFa4ViJ8/s1600/slider_problem.png>

This is a problem unique to windows 8.1 because the same code puts input_sliders below the plot correctly in Ubuntu 14.04.2 64 bit (in virtualbox) . Is there anything I should do to make this work on Windows 8.1? Rstudio version is 0.98.1103 and the session information is as follows.

messages.subject: ggvis categorical bar plot with fill
messages.subject_clean: ggvis categorical bar plot with fill
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have been using ggplot2 for several years now, and I am trying to make the switch from ggplot2 to ggvis(). However, I cannot find how to make a categorical bar plot. Any help in the right direction would be greatly appreciated, thanks! James

#### R Code ####
needed_packages <- c("ggvis", "dplyr", "data.table", "ggplot2")
sapply(needed_packages, require, character.only=TRUE)

dt_1 <-
  data.table(
    group = c(rep("a", 3), rep("b", 3), rep("c", 3)),
    frequency = sample(15:30, replace=TRUE, size=9),
    year = c(rep(2011:2013, 3))
    )

# this is what I was doing in ggplot2, which I want to do exactly the same way in ggvis
ggplot(data=dt_1, aes(x=group, y=frequency, fill=factor(year) ) )+
  geom_bar(stat="identity", position=position_dodge(0.5), width=0.5, color="black")

# works
dt_1 %>%
  ggvis(~group, ~frequency, fill = ~factor(year) ) %>%
  layer_points()

# empty graph???
dt_1 %>%
  ggvis(~group, ~frequency ) %>%
  layer_rects()

# works - seems to be close to what I want
dt_1 %>%
  ggvis(~group, ~frequency ) %>%
  layer_bars()

# does not work - wish it did like the layer_points above
dt_1 %>%
  ggvis(~group, ~frequency, fill = ~factor(year) ) %>%
  layer_bars()

# does not work, seems that only numeric x and y vectors allowed
dt_1 %>% ggvis(~group, ~frequency, fill := "#fff8dc") %>%
  layer_histograms()

messages.subject: Problem with linked-brush
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I’ve recently been playing around with shiny and ggvis after taking a break from it. PS. The MOOC data products course really helped to spark my interest in it again.

So I’ve gone about creating a shiny app <https://etheleon.shinyapps.io/GraphUI/>

and am playing with the linked_brush function to connect two plots
the scatter plot
the network diagram which i hacked together in ggvis using layer_paths()

now if you brush the data points on the scatter plot, it’ll cause its network counterpart to turn yellow and grow in size

However, I’m running into a problem when the number of points increase and it seems ggvis’s linked_brush function isnt capturing the selected data points.
You can see this by choosing path:ko01110: Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites

Any ideas guys?

Havent tried just plotting the two outside of shiny.

messages.subject: linked brushing with reactive plots does not update
messages.subject_clean: linked brushing with reactive plots does not update
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

First off I'd like to say ggvis is awesome and I am very thankful for this tool.

However I am experiencing issues when trying to use linked brushing with a reactive data set. Basically, which points are selected does not reset when new data is piped in and the ggvis plot is redrawn. Any advice on how to fix this or a suggested work around is much appreciated. Please see code below, which is also at https://gist.github.com/dgrapov/e1712017fe6a92b48eaf .

Thanks,
-Dmitry

library
library(ggvis)

shinyApp(
  ui =bootstrapPage(
    actionButton("randomize", "Randomize"),
    ggvisOutput("plot1"),
    ggvisOutput("plot2"),
    verbatimTextOutput("summary")
  ),

  server=function(input, output, session) {

    main.data<-cocaine # staring data

    get_data<-reactive({
      input$randomize # need this for data update
      cocaine <- main.data[sample(1:nrow(main.data),20), ]
      cocaine$id <- seq_len(nrow(cocaine))
      return(cocaine)
    })

  observe({
    #new data
    cocaine <- get_data()

    lb <- linked_brush(keys = cocaine$id, "red") # does not reset after data update

    cocaine %>%
      ggvis(~weight, ~price, key := ~id) %>%
      layer_points(fill := lb$fill, fill.brush := "red", opacity := 0.3) %>%
      lb$input() %>%
      set_options(width = 300, height = 300) %>%
      bind_shiny("plot1") # Very important!

    # A subset of cocaine, of only the selected points
      selected <- lb$selected

    cocaine_selected <- reactive({
      input$randomize
      cocaine[selected(), ]
    })

    cocaine %>%
      ggvis(~potency) %>%
      layer_histograms(width = 5, boundary = 0) %>%
      add_data(cocaine_selected) %>%
      layer_histograms(width = 5, boundary = 0, fill := "#dd3333") %>%
      set_options(width = 300, height = 300) %>%
      bind_shiny("plot2")

      #summary of selected (Selected does not react)
      output$summary<-renderPrint({
        matrix(selected())
      })
    })
  }
)
